newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end quiet trade mostly firmer.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end quiet trade mostly firmer.

text.p: Quiet range-trade left most IMM currencies firmer, as action centered on cash crosses.
Yen sagged again late, however, with one fund seen selling 500 December futures at the close, floor brokers said.
The contract earlier cut its biggest losses after respecting technical support pegged at the $0.009196 level, or 110.05, and the pit-session's low.

Some brokers tied yen's downturn partly to its inability to followthrough on Wednesday's sharp rally, which a large drop in open interest had suggested consisted of shortcovering rather than fresh position-taking.

December marks settled into tight price bands, holding support near $0.6632, also last Friday's low. Sterling firmed but stayed below 1.5560, the level where large sell stops were hit Thursday. And Canadian dollar rose but stayed below resistance pegged at $0.7343, a chartist added.
Brokers said pressure on marks stemmed from "convergence" trades as cash players sold marks for other European units, such as French francs, Italian lira and Spanish peseta.
Heading into Friday's and Saturday's meeting in Dublin of European Union finance ministers, brokers said they decided to view the possibility of the union in a more positive light.
The talks were expected to focus on a budget stability pact among EMU participants, a new exchange rate mechanism linking the single currency to non-members, and legal details.
Focus turned back to Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, with the market expected to prove thin on Monday because a Japanese holiday.

The Swiss franc also gained ground on marks, with brokers saying comments by Swiss National Bank directorate member Bruno Gehrig may have added some lift but seemed at odds with other actions by the Swiss central bank.

Gehrig said a sustained drop in the Swiss franc over the long term would be a "disastrous risk" to Swiss price stability. He also said SNB's principle strategy for bolstering the sluggish economic was to continue to provide liquidity to the Swiss money markets.
But analysts said Swiss inflation already was low and that SNB has added liquidity to temper the Swiss unit's strength.

Dec yen fell $0.000045 to $0.009205, marks off $0.0010 at $0.6636, Swiss francs rose $0.0024 to $0.8141, pound up $0.0026 at $1.5546, Can dollar rose $0.0022 to $0.7342, Aus dollar rose $0.0010 to $0.7899, Mex peso down $0.000350 at $0.125525. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
